\caption{\textbf{Each stage buys a different thing.} Averages over 24 objects and every
arm on each rung. Adapting the frozen generator's cross-attention alone recovers most of
both quantities: +11.97\,dB of PSNR and 58.8\% of the texel flicker.
Extending the adapter to self-attention adds +1.03\,dB of fidelity but
almost no coherence (1.7\% flicker, 2.3\% acceleration): it is a
fidelity stage, not a temporal one. Temporal context is the reverse --- it lowers flicker a further
15.8\% and acceleration 32.9\% while PSNR moves only
+0.07\,dB, for a total of 65.9\% and
75.2\% against the baseline. Drift is a guard rather than a score, so no
best value is marked: it is flat across the two adapted rows (+0.4\%),
confirming the coherence gain is not bought by damping the texture toward a still image ---
the degenerate solution that minimises both other metrics. Rungs 27--30 carry no temporal
term (28--30 add KL regularisers to rung~27); the temporal set is rungs 31--34 together with
every arm using the temporal blend ($+$M).}
